name: SVM / similarity kernel
short: A pairwise function whose Gram matrices are PSD.
body: For a real symmetric kernel k, every finite Gram matrix must be positive semidefinite. This makes k representable as an inner product in a feature space.
example: The ordinary dot product is a kernel: k(x,y)=xᵀy. More elaborate kernels let algorithms use implicit feature spaces.
note: A plausible similarity score is not automatically a valid PSD kernel. Literature often says positive definite while allowing semidefinite Gram matrices.

name: Gaussian / RBF similarity kernel
short: Exponentially decreasing similarity in squared distance.
body: The Gaussian radial-basis-function kernel compares points using their squared Euclidean distance and a scale parameter. It is a standard PSD kernel.
example: At distance ℓ, similarity is e⁻¹/²≈0.607. At zero distance it is 1.
note: The same Gaussian shape appears in heat flow, KDE and image blur. Their arguments, units and normalization differ.

name: Covariance kernel
short: The covariance between indexed random variables.
body: A covariance kernel expresses how fluctuations at two inputs co-vary. For a Gaussian process, a mean function and a valid covariance kernel specify all finite-dimensional distributions.
example: A long length scale in an RBF covariance makes nearby observations strongly correlated; a shorter scale allows faster variation.
note: A covariance may be negative at some pairs while its Gram matrices remain PSD. Positive entrywise values and positive semidefiniteness are different properties.

sources.title: Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning: covariance functions

name: Neural tangent kernel
body: For a scalar network output, the NTK compares gradients of the output with respect to model parameters. It describes local function changes during training.
example: For fθ(x)=θx, the NTK is xy. For a finite nonlinear network, it generally changes as θ changes.
note: The limiting constant-kernel training description requires specific infinite-width assumptions. An arbitrary finite network is not automatically in that regime.

sources.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization

name: Reproducing kernel
short: A pairwise function that reproduces evaluation.
body: In a reproducing kernel Hilbert space, evaluation is an inner product with a distinguished kernel section. Every positive-semidefinite kernel determines an associated RKHS.
example: If k(x,y)=xy on ℝ, the associated functions have the form f(x)=ax; pairing with k(x,·) recovers ax.
note: Not every Hilbert space of functions is an RKHS: point evaluation must be a bounded functional.

name: Attention kernel / feature map
short: A pairwise weighting expressed using kernel features.
body: Kernel formulations of attention express pairwise weights through feature maps. Associativity can then rearrange some attention computations to avoid explicitly forming every pairwise weight.
example: A nonnegative feature map can give usable attention weights, followed by row normalization and a weighted sum of value vectors.
note: Distinct query/key projections and row normalization generally do not produce a symmetric PSD token matrix. Not every attention score is a Mercer kernel.

name: Quantum feature kernel
short: Similarity defined by encoded quantum states.
body: A quantum feature map encodes an input into a state. A common kernel is the squared overlap of two encoded states, also interpretable as an inner product of density operators.
example: Identical pure states give similarity 1; orthogonal states give 0.
note: This is a kernel method implemented or estimated with quantum circuits. A useful quantum advantage does not follow merely from the definition.

sources.title: Supervised learning with quantum enhanced feature spaces

name: Bergman kernel
short: The reproducing kernel for square-integrable holomorphic functions.
body: The Bergman kernel reproduces holomorphic functions in an L² space on a complex domain and represents the Bergman projection.
example: On the unit disk with ordinary area measure, integrating B(z,w)f(w) over the disk recovers f(z) for suitable holomorphic f.
note: The domain and measure normalization determine the formula. It is both an integral kernel and a reproducing kernel.

name: Determinantal / correlation kernel
short: A kernel whose determinants encode joint point correlations.
body: Determinantal point processes express their correlation functions as determinants of matrices built from a kernel. Famous scaling limits include the sine, Airy and Bessel kernels.
example: The sine kernel is sin(π(x−y))/(π(x−y)), with diagonal value 1, in a common bulk-scaling convention.
note: Not every PSD kernel defines a valid determinantal process. Operator constraints and the reference measure also matter.

sources.title: Random point fields and random matrices

name: Fisher kernel
body: A generative model provides score features: gradients of log likelihood with respect to its parameters. The Fisher kernel compares those features using an information-based metric.
example: Two observations are similar when they suggest similar parameter changes in the chosen generative model.
note: The model and parameterization are part of the construction; an inverse or suitable generalized inverse requires care.

sources.title: Exploiting Generative Models in Discriminative Classifiers

name: Graph kernel: machine learning
short: A similarity kernel between whole graphs.
body: Graph kernels use features such as walks, subgraphs or neighborhood patterns to compare graph-structured inputs within kernel methods.
example: A simple kernel compares vectors counting vertex labels. Richer kernels compare shared walks or Weisfeiler–Lehman patterns.
note: A graph-theory kernel is a selected vertex set in a single digraph; a graph ML kernel compares two graph objects.

name: Kernel mean / distribution embedding
short: Represent a distribution by an average kernel section.
body: A kernel mean embedding averages feature representations under a distribution. Distances between such embeddings produce the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD).
example: With a linear kernel, the embedding captures the ordinary mean. A characteristic kernel can distinguish all probability distributions in an appropriate class.
note: Kernel here is still the underlying pairwise PSD function; the mean embedding is a derived object. Moment and measurability assumptions apply.

name: Named similarity-kernel families
short: Different constructions inside the PSD family.
body: Linear, polynomial, Laplacian, Matérn, rational-quadratic and periodic kernels encode different notions of features, smoothness or repetition.
example: For γ=1, c=0 and d=2, the polynomial kernel equals the dot product of quadratic feature vectors.
note: Parameters and domains matter. The sigmoid formula tanh(γxᵀy+c), although offered by software APIs, is not PSD for arbitrary parameters.

sources.title: Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning: covariance functions

name: Neural-network GP kernel
short: Output covariance from a random network.
body: Randomly initialized networks can induce covariance kernels. Under suitable infinite-width conditions, their outputs converge to a Gaussian process with a network-dependent kernel.
example: For fθ(x)=θx with θ∼N(0,1), the induced covariance is xy.
note: The NNGP kernel uses random outputs; the NTK uses parameter gradients. Their roles and formulas differ.

sources.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization

name: Stein kernel: pairwise discrepancy
short: An RKHS kernel transformed by Stein operators.
body: Applying a distribution's Stein operator to both arguments of a base kernel produces a pairwise kernel used to assess sample fit, often without a density's normalizing constant.
example: A kernel Stein discrepancy combines density scores and derivatives of an RBF kernel to compare a sample with a model.
note: This pairwise function is distinct from the one-input integration-by-parts Stein kernel τ(x). Boundary and regularity conditions matter.

sources.title: A Kernelized Stein Discrepancy for Goodness-of-fit Tests

name: String / sequence kernel
short: An inner-product comparison of sequence features.
body: String kernels compare sequences through features such as counts of substrings or subsequences, often without explicitly constructing the full feature vectors.
example: For length-2 substring counts, AABA has AA, AB and BA once each. Comparing these counts gives a simple spectrum kernel.
note: This is a similarity function for sequences, not a text-processing routine or language runtime.

name: Szegő kernel
short: A reproducing kernel for a Hardy-space setting.
body: The Szegő kernel reproduces functions in a Hardy space, using boundary rather than area-based data in the standard disk setting.
example: With normalized boundary measure dθ/(2π), the disk Hardy-space kernel is 1/(1−z w̄).
note: Normalization varies. The Szegő and Bergman kernels reproduce different function spaces; they are not interchangeable.

sources.title: A Szegő Kernel for Discrete Series
